Elle est soumise aux dispositions des articles L. 2124-2, R. 2124-2 1° et R. 2161-2 à R. 2161-5 du Code de la commande publique. 1.3 - Type et forme de contrat Les lots 1 à 5 sont des accords-cadres à bons de commande, conclus avec un montant maximum fixé pour chaque lot, en application des articles L. 2125-1 1°, R. 2162-1 à R. 2162-6, R. 2162-13 et R. 2162-14 du Code de la commande publique. Ils donnent lieu à l'émission de bons de commande. Chaque accord-cadre sera attribué à un seul opérateur économique. Le lot 6 n'est pas exécuté par bons de commande et ne donne lieu à aucun paiement de la CCI. Le titulaire se rémunère sur les recettes publicitaires qu'il facture et encaisse auprès des annonceurs, et reverse à la CCI une redevance dans les conditions fixé es au CCP. La valeur estimée du lot 6, correspondant au chiffre d'affaires publicitaire prévisionnel sur la durée maximale du contrat, est de 180 000 € HT. Le montant de l'avance est fixé à 5,00 % du montant du bon de commande si la durée de son exécution est inférieure ou égale à douze mois ; si cette durée est supérieure à douze mois, l'avance est égale à 5,00 % d'une somme égale à douze fois le montant du bon de commande divisé par cette durée exprimée en mois. L’intervention des cordistes est interdite et nécessite l’utilisation d’une nacelle automotrice pilotée par des personnels certifiés munis de moyens de protection individuelle normalisés. (Voir article “ Etablissement des Plans de prévention des risques”) La méthode de pose est la s

isée suivant les mesures de prévention indiqué au plan de prévention, à l’écart de la circulation du public. La pose de filets de protection n’est pas nécessaire. La circulation de la nacelle sur Piazza se fait par la voie de circulation dite « Pompier ». 2.2.2.3- - Dépose/Pose des bâches (B) de la BO.3a et BO.3b : Même caractéristique que la méthode de dépose /pose (article 2.2.2.1) Ces bâches sont fixées sur une structure existante composée de quatre câbles gainés fixés sur une structure métallique rigide. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

C.1.1 Eligibility: To be eligible to participate in the medical plan, LE Staff (both full time and part time) must be: -- Paid under the terms of the Local Compensation Plan (LCP); and – -- Under a non-temporary direct hire appointment, personal services agreement (PSA), or personal services contract (PSC); or -- Under a temporary direct hire appointment or PSA Fixed Term of one year or more. C.1.2 Riders: There are no riders under this contract. C.1.3 Periods of Ineligibility: Employees and their dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment for which premiums are not paid. Additionally, employee's dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment during which the employee was not eligible to participate. During a period of extended Leave Without Pay (LWOP) or other unpaid leave beyond one pay period, the employee is responsible for the full cost of the insurance premiums for self and dependents. The Mission will pay the premiums directly to the Contractor and will collect the full cost from the employee on a quarterly basis. Alternatively

The ARB is the official body providing design review for the Office of the Architect of the Capitol, but the Architect of the Capitol retains sole authority for final design approval. ARB review covers planning, design, appearance, and visibility of projects designed by consulting architects, in-house designers, and other parties. ARB review applies to third-party entities, not under contract to, or directly supervised by the Architect of the Capitol including, but not limited to, legislative branch agencies and public utilities. Branch is responsible for soliciting and awarding AOC procurements for architect, engineering, construction management and construction services exceeding $100,000. Service & Supply Branch is responsible for soliciting and awarding AOC procurements for commodities and services (excluding AE and Construction Management) exceeding $100,000 and all GSA actions exceeding $1,000,000. The Small Purchase Branch awards AOC procurements of $100,000 or less and GSA actions less than $1,000,000. Applicability of Laws and Statutes: The procurement authority for AOC is established by statute codified at 2 U.S.C. § 1801 et seq. As a legislative branch agency, AOC is not required to follow the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). However, AOC does incorporate certain FAR clauses and provisions in its solicitations and follows the regulatory guidance found in the FAR to the maximum extent possible. The AOC’s formal guidelines are established in AOC Order 34-1, Contracting Manual. For procurements of $100,000 or less ("small purchases"), the AOC uses small purchase procedures implemented through policy signed by the Architect. Procurements exceeding $5,000 up to $100,000 are normally provided by small businesses utilizing the AOC small business set-aside program i
